items.text: The wheel was invented thousands of years ago and changed how people travel.
items.explanation: The oldest known wheels date from around 3500 BC. Wheeled carts soon made it easier to move people and heavy loads.

items.text: Ancient Egyptians built huge stone pyramids as tombs for their kings.
items.explanation: The pyramids served as royal tombs. The Great Pyramid of Giza, built around 2600 BC, was made for King Khufu.

items.text: The Berlin Wall divided East and West Berlin from 1961 until it was opened on 9 November 1989, and Germany reunified in 1990.
items.explanation: The wall was built on 13 August 1961 by East Germany. After it opened in 1989, Germany was reunified on 3 October 1990.

items.text: Christopher Columbus crossed the Atlantic in 1492 with three ships, the Nina, the Pinta, and the Santa Maria, sailing for Spain.
items.explanation: Columbus landed in the Bahamas in October 1492. His first voyage was funded by the Spanish crown and he sailed with three ships.

items.text: The Magna Carta, sealed by King John of England in 1215, limited the power of the king and is a landmark in the history of law.
items.explanation: The charter said that even the king had to follow the law. It was first issued in June 1215 at Runnymede.
